title: Write the aim state
summary: Add AIM, the PID, the angle to the goal, isAimed and the command.

say.never:
The drivetrain already has two states, `ARCADE` and `IDLE`. You will give it a third, `AIM`: while the left bumper is held, the robot spins on the spot until it faces the goal.

You will do six things, in this order: 1) add the new state, 2) make a PID controller that turns the robot, 3) work out which way the goal is, 4) write what the `AIM` state does each loop, 5) write the yes/no `isAimed` method, 6) write the command the button starts.

You are done when the robot spins toward the goal on the left bumper. The checkpoints read your code. Tuning comes after.

say.never:
To face the goal, the robot needs a turning command that gets smaller as it lines up. A **PID controller** makes that from the **error**: how far the robot's heading is from the direction it wants. It has three terms.

- **P** pushes in proportion to the error: far off, big push.
- **I** adds up the error that is left over time, to finish the last bit. Too much makes it wind up.
- **D** reacts to how fast the error is changing, to calm things down before it overshoots.

The constants hold the three gains. The controller also needs two settings: **headings wrap around** (359 degrees and -1 degree are the same direction, so it should take the short way round), and a **tolerance** (how close counts as aimed). It works in radians.
say.bit: A PID turns the error (how far off the heading is) into a turn command: P in proportion, I for leftover error, D to calm it. It needs wrap-around and a tolerance, in radians.

say.never:
The **error** needs two directions: where the robot faces, and where the goal is.

The direction to the goal is the arrow from the robot to the goal: take the goal's position and subtract the robot's. The angle of that arrow is the direction you want to face. `getAngleToGoal()` should return it.

Use the robot's **estimated** pose, the one from the vision work. A robot can only aim from where it thinks it is, and that is why the vision work matters.
say.bit: The direction to the goal is the angle of the arrow from the robot to the goal. Use the estimated pose.

say.never:
Each loop, the `AIM` case does two things: it asks the PID for a turn command from the robot's heading and the angle to the goal, and it hands that turn to the drive with no forward speed so the robot **spins on the spot**.

**Which way is positive?** Headings count positive counter-clockwise, but the drive's turn command can point the other way, so the PID's answer has to be flipped. If the robot spins away from the goal, check this first.

The other states must also **reset** the controller. Otherwise old error and old buildup from the last aim carry into the next one.
say.bit: The AIM case feeds heading and goal angle to the PID and spins the robot on the spot. The turn sign may need flipping. Other states reset the PID.

steps.title: The AIM case and the resets

say.never:
Add `case AIM:` to the switch. Set `aim_turn_ = -aim_pid_.calculate(heading, angleToGoal);` where the heading is `getPose().getRotation().getRadians()` and the angle is `getAngleToGoal().getRadians()`. The minus sign is the flip. Then call `drive_.arcadeDrive(0.0, aim_turn_);` so the robot spins on the spot, and end the case with `break;`.

Also add `aim_pid_.reset();` to the `ARCADE` and `IDLE` cases. Click **I did it** when the AIM case and both resets are written.

say.never:
`isAimed()` answers a yes/no question, and two things must both be true: the heading error is inside the tolerance, **and** the robot has stopped turning. A robot that is swinging through the goal is not aimed, even for a moment.

The tolerance comes from the constants, and the heading error is in radians, so convert before comparing it.

The command at the end is the same shape as the shoot command: it sets the wanted state to `AIM` when the button goes down and back to `ARCADE` when it is released.
say.bit: isAimed needs both a small heading error and a stopped robot. The command sets AIM on press and ARCADE on release.

say.never:
Hold the **left bumper** (**E** on the keyboard). The robot should spin toward the goal, which starts about 45 degrees to its left. It probably won't stop in the right place yet, and that's fine.

If it spins the wrong way, check the sign flip. If nothing happens, check the binding and that the state is `AIM` in AdvantageScope.

Then tune **by hand**, one gain at a time. Start with only P: raise it until the robot turns briskly, lower it if it swings back and forth. If it overshoots, add a little D. Leave I at zero unless it stops just short of the goal. Change one number, Start again, and try again.
say.bit: Hold the left bumper. It should spin toward the goal. If it spins the wrong way, flip the sign. Tune by hand: P first, a little D to stop overshoot, I last.
